title: The Attack on Pearl Harbor
subtitle: Hawaii · 25 November – 8 December 1941
tz: Hawaii time · UTC−10:30 (Tokyo is 19½ hours ahead)
footnote: Hawaii time (UTC−10:30). The Kido Butai's track is reconstructed from its operation orders and the TROMs' distance statements — no daily fixes were published; the launch point is 'about 230 miles north of Oahu'. Berths on Battleship Row are placed from the harbour chart; Ward's midget from the 2002 wreck survey. The loss counter counts only the ships sunk in the harbour (1,870 men); 2,403 Americans died in all, 55 Japanese airmen and nine submariners. Formation members are spread slightly so they don't overlap.

kdb.name: Vice Admiral Chūichi Nagumo
kdb.bio: Sceptical of the plan he was given, he brought six carriers 3,500 miles across the empty North Pacific undetected and launched 350 aircraft on schedule. Then, with the American carriers unlocated and his fuel low, he declined the third strike that Fuchida and Yamaguchi urged on him — and left the oil tanks, the dockyard and the submarine base untouched.

subs.name: Captain Hanku Sasaki
subs.bio: Five fleet submarines each carrying a two-man midget: launched ten miles off the harbour between midnight and 03:30. None of the five midgets returned; their one certain result was to give Ward the first shot of the war an hour before the aircraft arrived.

arizona.name: Admiral Husband E. Kimmel
arizona.bio: Had the fleet at its Sunday moorings, no long-range air search to the north and his carriers safely at sea by chance. Watched from his quarters as Arizona blew up; a spent bullet through the window struck his chest — 'it would have been merciful had it killed me'.
arizona.fate: Relieved 17 December 1941; reduced to rear admiral; died 1968 still contesting the verdict.

ward.name: Lieutenant William Outerbridge
ward.bio: Two days in command of a 1918 destroyer. Sank a midget submarine at 06:45 and reported it in plain terms — the message reached Kimmel at 07:40, fifteen minutes before the bombs.
ward.fate: Commanded O'Brien at Normandy and Leyte; Ward was sunk under him — by kamikaze, three years to the day later — and O'Brien scuttled her.

tf8.name: Vice Admiral William F. Halsey
tf8.role: Commander, Aircraft Battle Force — Task Force 8
tf8.bio: Sailed under war orders on 28 November — 'sink any shipping sighted, shoot down any plane encountered' — and was due back in Pearl on the 6th; the weather kept him out. His scouts flew into the raid; his afternoon strike chased a phantom.

tf12.name: Rear Admiral John H. Newton
tf12.bio: Ferrying Marine dive bombers to Midway; recalled to hunt for the Japanese carriers in the wrong direction.

strikes.name: Tone and Chikuma's floatplanes
strikes.note: Two Jakes scout Lahaina Roads (empty) and Pearl Harbor ahead of the strike; the American carriers are not there

strikes.name: First wave — Fuchida
strikes.note: 49 Kates with 800-kg armour-piercing bombs, 40 torpedo Kates, 51 Vals, 43 Zeros. 'Tora! Tora! Tora!' at 07:53; Arizona, Oklahoma, West Virginia, California and Utah hit within fifteen minutes. Nine aircraft lost

strikes.name: Second wave — Shimazaki
strikes.note: 54 Kates, 78 Vals, 35 Zeros against the airfields and the ships still fighting: Nevada, Pennsylvania in dock, Shaw, Curtiss. Twenty aircraft lost to the awakened AA

strikes.name: Enterprise's morning scouts
strikes.note: Eighteen Dauntlesses flying ahead to Ford Island arrive in the middle of the attack; seven shot down by Zeros and by American gunners, eight airmen killed

strikes.name: Enterprise's phantom strike
strikes.note: Launched against a reported carrier south of Oahu — nothing there. Six Wildcats diverted to Hickam after dark; three are shot down by friendly fire

torpedoes.note: Three hits in the first minutes, two more as she rolls; capsizes at 08:08 with 429 men
Seven torpedoes; counter-flooding keeps her upright as she settles
Two hits with her manholes open for inspection
The target ship, mistaken for a carrier — capsizes at 08:12
Kept afloat by a lighter and counter-flooding
Passes under Oglala into Helena; Oglala capsizes two hours later
One hit forward — she still gets under way
Both torpedoes miss Curtiss and explode ashore; Monaghan rams her seven minutes later

engagements.note: Two rounds from No. 3 gun at 50 yards; the second hits the conning tower
The fleet's AA guns — manned within minutes, they shoot down 29 aircraft over the morning
Curtiss and Monaghan fire on the midget's conning tower inside the harbour
Under way with every gun firing, the target of the second wave's dive bombers

Nagumo turns south at 24 knots, 400 miles north of Oahu

I-16 launches the first midget submarine
Condor sights a periscope off the entrance
First wave launched
Ward sinks a midget submarine — the first shots
Opana radar plots the first wave at 132 miles; 'don't worry about it'
Kaneohe strafed — the attack begins
'Tora! Tora! Tora!' — surprise achieved
Battleship Row torpedoed; 'Air raid Pearl Harbor. This is not drill'
Arizona's forward magazine explodes — 1,177 killed
Oklahoma capsizes
Utah capsizes
Enterprise's scouts fly into the battle
Monaghan rams a midget submarine inside the harbour
Second wave attacks
Nevada gets under way
Nevada beached at Hospital Point
Shaw's magazine explodes in the floating dock
The last aircraft leave; 2,403 Americans dead, 188 aircraft destroyed
Nagumo recovers his aircraft and declines a third strike

Roosevelt: 'a date which will live in infamy' — Congress declares war
Enterprise enters Pearl Harbor: 'Before we're through with 'em, the Japanese language will be spoken only in hell'
